text:
Anya: heads up — after NCCL 2.23.1 + CUDA 12.3 driver rollout to us-east1 GPU pool we started seeing intermittent all-reduce stalls and a 2-3x jump in p99 for multi-GPU inference on NVLink A100 nodes. Not full hangs but some collectives time out and retry. Anyone seen this? :eyes:

Diego: saw the same spike around 11:17 UTC. p99 from ~40ms -> ~120ms for our batch infer route. Affected runs show slight retry/noise, not constant failures.

Marie: tagging infra oncall @DevOps-Oncall — can you pause the driver rollout to other regions? We need a canary rollback. :warning:

DevOps-Oncall: pausing rollout now. I've cordoned the next 50 nodes in the rollout group. Starting investigation — will try to repro on a canary. If you have failing job ids paste them here.

Infra-bot: alert: bulk anomaly detected — cluster: us-east1-gpu-pool, metric: collective_latency_99, delta: +220%, samples: 56 clusters. Query: `SELECT host, job_id, op, p99_ms FROM metrics WHERE op LIKE '%allreduce%' AND region='us-east1' AND ts>NOW()-1h`

Oliver: pasting relevant dmesg / nccl logs from a node showing stall pattern:
```
[  123.456789] nvidia: nvlink: timeout waiting for peer response
NCCL WARN Call to allReduce timed out after 12000 ms
NCCL INFO Resetting transport for p2p between GPU0 GPU1
Traceback (most recent call last): ...
```

Sasha: repro notes — single-GPU ops not impacted. Confirmed only multi-GPU collectives on NVLink topologies. Also seeing more noise on >2 GPU jobs.

Diego: quick diff shows this lines up exactly with driver push + NCCL 2.23.1 artifacts. We'll try re-running the same job pinned to non-NVLink nodes to see if it clears.

Anya: mitigation proposals: 1) roll back driver to CUDA 12.2 on a canary and test; 2) pin critical inference routes to non-NVLink nodes or reduce collective sizes; 3) revert to NCCL 2.22.x if rollback doesn't help. Which should we prioritize?

DevOps-Oncall: starting rollback to 12.2 on canary set (10 nodes). Commands I'm using: 
```
 gcloud compute ssh gpu-node-12 --command "sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-515 && sudo reboot"
 kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
```
ETA ~30m for canary. I'll report perf after the node reboots and we rerun a smoke job.

Marie: created ticket INF-3421 with perf traces and added eng-runtime + infra teams. Please attach flamegraphs if you have them.

Oliver: one more thing — kernel version on some nodes is 5.19.7; there are known NVLink driver interactions there. dmesg shows `nvlink: reset failed` intermittently. Keeping that in mind while we test rollbacks.

Anya: thanks. If rollback on canary clears the regression we should stop the NCCL 2.23.1 rollout and coordinate with ML infra to get a rebuild with NVLink fixes.

DevOps-Oncall: canary results: after rolling back driver -> CUDA 12.2 and booting, collected a few runs — p99 back to baseline (~45ms), no all-reduce timeouts in 30m window. Reverting rollout across remaining us-east1 nodes.

Sasha: good catch. For immediate safety I've updated pod scheduling rule to avoid NVLink nodes for the critical inference route until we have a validated driver/NCCL combo.

Diego: adding perf regression checks to the CI that will fail merges if collective p99 increases >30% vs baseline for our heavy routes.

Marie: next steps: 1) block NCCL 2.23.1 in model-serving images until we validate; 2) open an upstream CI with microbenchmarks for NVLink topologies; 3) schedule postmortem tomorrow 10:00am PT.

Anya: filing postmortem and owners. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
